newsitem.title: USA: FTC chairman says Staples deal fixable.
newsitem.headline: FTC chairman says Staples deal fixable.

text.p: Federal Trade Comission Chairman Robert Pitofsky said Thursday the proposed deal between Staples Inc and Office Depot Inc is potentially "fixable," and his agency will act within 10 to 14 days on the new merger proposal.
"Yes it's fixable," Pitofsky said when asked by a reporter if the original merger plan -- which had been turned down by the commission -- could be altered so that it would win approval.
But he said he had not seen the new plan.
"I'm really just speculating here, I don't know what they're offering or what we would require," he said.
He added that the commission would likely act relatively quickly. "There's no reason for us to sit around with this for more than 10 days, two weeks, something like that," he said.

The commission voted 4-1 last week to reject the proposed merger. A few days later, the two stores reached an agreement in principle to divest 63 stores to the third player in the office superstore field, OfficeMax.
